name: Sara Usman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. We keep your answers confidential. What is a usual workday for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage four people who arrange staff training for a large supermarket group. We book induction sessions, check completion records and chase stores when a new worker has not had safety instruction. I have a bachelor’s degree and moved from being a store trainer into this junior manager job this year; the national calendar and budget reports still trip me up. I use an approved AI tool once in a while to draft reminders, then check the dates against the store rota.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like right now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works as a paramedic, and our children are nine and fourteen. We have a mortgage, almost nine months of expenses saved and pay that is high for this manager role because the national schedule includes evening launches. There are plenty of comparable operations and training jobs nearby. My partner’s shifts change often, so any new job has to work with the children’s pickups.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the planners AI Plateau is a small change to reminders and record checks. A store still needs a real trainer in the room before a new worker uses a heavy pallet jack.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my pay and the team are safe if AI only tidies routine messages. My partner’s shifts can upset the family calendar, but we have savings and a good salary. I would rather fix our own scheduling mistakes than buy another tool for them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the Friday call with store trainers and check every missed safety session against the actual rota. If a small new reminder feature arrives, I’d try it with last term’s missed classes before letting it send messages. We would continue adding money to our savings account each payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and bills. The calendar is messy, but this picture does not change what a new worker needs to learn.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a reminder miss recently?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A new worker was marked trained because the class was booked, but the person had been on sick leave. The store trainer spotted it before a pallet jack shift. Booking and attendance are two different things.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you tell your partner about the calendar?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We put both shift rotas on the fridge each Sunday. Our older child can get home alone, but the nine-year-old still needs an adult. We check that before I agree to an evening launch.

say: **AI Plateau** may tidy reminders but cannot confirm a real class happened.
A store trainer still checks **attendance** before risky equipment work.
think: My **pay and team** feel safe if only routine messages change.
My partner’s **shift rota** remains the practical family problem.
do: **Keep** Friday calls with store trainers and check missed classes.
**Test** the reminder feature on last term’s absences before live use.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and bills in this mild picture.
S0.quote: Booking and attendance are two different things.
fieldNote: Her **nine-month reserve** and high salary make a routine tool feel manageable.
She separates **class booking** from a worker’s actual attendance and safe use of equipment.

steps.text: Keep Friday calls and verify missed safety classes against store rotas
Test reminder feature on last term missed classes before live use
Continue transferring money into savings from each payday

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will write reminders, plan sessions, check records and answer basic staff questions. Store workers should have a say before the company raises targets for a smaller planning team.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Most of my new desk role is the work the card names. I know how to teach in a store, but I am still learning to manage this office, and the group may decide it needs fewer planning managers. My partner’s wage and our savings give us time, not a promise of a replacement role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d run a comparison of booked sessions and actual attendance in six stores, using the approved AI tool only to flag gaps. I’d ask the staff council to bring trainer workloads and paid redeployment into the next meeting. If my office is reduced, I’d apply for open regional trainer roles only if the pay is enough for our mortgage and the hours fit pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the manager post. I could teach again, but I cannot assume a regional vacancy will open when I need it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the six-store comparison show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How many workers were booked, attended and then still needed a second session. I would ask each trainer to confirm the attendance sheet. A clean online record is not proof that the person learnt the task.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why bring the staff council in?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A planner and a store trainer both carry the extra work when a system misses someone. We should set targets with their evidence, not just my manager report. I would bring the six-store numbers to the council.

say: **Training automation** needs worker input before planning targets rise across stores.
I would compare **attendance** with booked sessions and show trainers where the records miss a real class.
think: My new office post could shrink because much of it is **screen planning**.
Savings and my partner’s wage buy time, but a **trainer vacancy** is uncertain.
do: **Compare** bookings and attendance in six stores this quarter.
**Bring** trainer workloads and paid redeployment to the staff council.
**Apply** for regional trainer posts only if pay and pickup hours work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about the manager post and uncertain openings.
S1.quote: A clean online record is not proof that the person learnt the task.
fieldNote: She uses an **attendance comparison** to see where the AI misses a worker, not to promise job security.
The **staff council** is a route for store trainers as well as central planners.

steps.text: Compare AI flagged bookings with trainer-confirmed attendance in six stores
Bring workload and paid redeployment evidence to the staff council
Apply for regional trainer vacancies only if pay and pickups fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could arrange training, check records and write every reminder without our office. We should ask for a staffing date and funded routes for workers who want to teach in stores.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 threatens my office and the planning part of a regional trainer job. Robots able to do hands-on store work come around 2031, so the physical demonstrations may change later. I expect the central team to shrink and my junior manager post could go. Nine months saved gives us a chance to search, but the mortgage still runs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I’d ask the staff council to seek written cut dates and paid redeployment terms. I’d compare three advertised store-training roles with our mortgage and childcare costs, and apply if the school pickup hours fit. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose my post, I’d take a confirmed teaching role rather than keep paying for a management title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I have options, but the staff with little savings would face the same cut with far less time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach in a store?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Safe handling of the pallet jack, stock-room checks and what to do when a customer falls. I have taught those before, though I would need to refresh the equipment rules. I would not claim teaching is immune to later robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say I may work in a store again, not that we have to leave our home. My partner and I can cover the mortgage while I look. We would only change childcare after I had an actual rota.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates and funded paths into store teaching.
I would not promise the central office **survives**.
think: My planning work faces AGI in **2028**; hands-on store robots follow around 2031.
My junior post could go, though **nine months saved** allows a search.
do: **Ask** the staff council next month for cut and redeployment terms.
**Apply** for posted store-training roles only if pay and school pickup fit.
**Take** a confirmed teaching offer after 2028 if my office post ends.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my post and colleagues with less savings.
S2.quote: Nine months saved gives us a chance to search, but the mortgage still runs.
fieldNote: She separates **2028 office risk** from later physical training changes around 2031.
Her **reserve and local openings** keep job loss manageable, while childcare hours constrain choices.

steps.text: Ask staff council for written cut dates and paid redeployment terms
Apply for store trainer posts only if salary covers mortgage childcare and pickup fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 leaves five years to test which teaching sessions still need a person at the store. The company should offer trainers paid practice with new equipment, not an unpaid course link.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My office scheduling could go in 2031, and the planning side of store training is exposed then too. Robots for hands-on work follow around 2034; that gives physical demonstrations a little more time but no guarantee forever. I could move back to teaching, but only if a real post remains and the rota works for home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January 2027 I’d propose a four-store pilot where I teach one real safety session at each store and compare attendance with the online plan. I’d take paid refresher training on the new equipment if the company provides cover for my office. After 2031, I’d apply for a regional trainer vacancy only if it has live teaching, pays our mortgage and fits the family shift rota when our younger child is about fourteen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the five years lets me test whether I still teach well. A course alone would not tell me whether I can teach safe pallet-jack use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you look for in that pilot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether a new worker can actually stop a pallet jack safely, not merely recite the rule. I would ask the store trainer to watch and tell me where my instruction is rusty. I have been in an office for several months.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the director says you cannot leave the office?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would propose one store first and ask for named cover for my planners. I would not leave my four people with a broken national timetable. The pilot needs paid work time and an agreed date.

say: **Five years** allows live teaching trials with paid cover.
A course alone cannot show **safe handling** on the store floor.
think: Office and training plans face **2031 AGI**, before hands-on robots around 2034.
A regional trainer role needs a **real vacancy** and a family-compatible rota.
do: **Teach** safety sessions in a four-store pilot from January 2027 if cover is approved.
**Take** paid equipment refresher training with office cover.
**Apply** after 2031 only for live-teaching posts with mortgage pay and workable family shifts.
feel: I feel **anxious**, with time to test my teaching skill.
S3.quote: A course alone would not tell me whether I can teach safe pallet-jack use.
fieldNote: Her **four-store pilot** tests actual safe handling and her own teaching skill rather than mere attendance records.
The **office cover** and family shift rota are explicit conditions on training and a future post.

steps.text: Teach four real store safety sessions if paid office cover is approved
Take paid equipment refresher training only with office cover
Apply after 2031 for live trainer role only with mortgage pay and workable family shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to agree on real job paths. The company should publish training hours, wages and how many people actually move into store posts each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older then, and if both wages hold we could pay down more of the mortgage. My central planning work still faces thinking AI in 2036; store training has planning too, and hands-on robots follow around 2039. I can prepare for a teaching role, but I will not count one before seeing a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I’d continue Friday trainer calls and increase the household savings transfer only after a full-pay month with childcare covered. I’d ask the staff council to review actual store-trainer openings annually. Before 2036 I’d take a paid in-store teaching assignment if offered with my salary and a workable rota; after AGI arrives I’d keep that role only while it still includes paid live instruction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy. A decade lets us plan, but the company has to show real jobs rather than a hopeful slide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why increase savings now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner has been picking up extra shifts, but that can change. I would add fifty only after both paychecks arrive and the childcare bill is paid. I would skip a month rather than use the credit card to claim we saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the store post pays less?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would run the numbers with my partner. A small reduction might work after the mortgage falls, but we cannot promise that now. I would not accept an assignment until the pay and rota are in writing.

say: A **decade** calls for published wages, training hours and actual placements.
I would ask the staff council to check **real store vacancies** each year.
think: Both wages could reduce the **mortgage** before 2036.
Central and trainer planning face **2036 AGI**, before store robots around 2039.
do: **Add** fifty to savings only after both paychecks and childcare costs clear.
**Take** a paid in-store teaching assignment with protected salary and rota, and keep it after 2036 only with paid live instruction.
feel: I feel **uneasy** until real jobs and pay are published.
S4.quote: I would skip a month rather than use the credit card to claim we saved.
fieldNote: Her **extra saving** depends on both paychecks and childcare bills, not an assumed future surplus.
She keeps **store teaching** conditional on a paid assignment, salary and rota in writing.

steps.text: Keep Friday calls with store trainers through 2026
Add fifty to savings only after both paychecks and childcare clear
Ask staff council annually for real store trainer vacancies
Take teaching assignment with full pay and rota; stay after 2036 only with paid live instruction

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the central office could shrink before I have tested a store teaching role. A written cut date, paid teaching time and a real vacancy with a rota my family can manage would help. Nine months saved lets us choose, but it cannot create an opening.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the new worker whether the training made the pallet jack feel safe. A completed online record is easy to print. A person steering a heavy load past another person needs practice.

headlineQuote: A person steering a heavy load past another person needs practice.
portrait: **Sara, 43**, recently moved from store training to a junior national training-office manager at a large supermarket group.
Her **high pay**, paramedic partner, nine-month reserve and local openings support a mortgage and two school-age children.
She uses **AI occasionally**, checks attendance with store trainers and is still learning the national calendar and budget.
She is **calm** under AI Plateau, anxious about faster office cuts and tests live teaching with paid cover and childcare conditions.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink her central office before she tests a store teaching role.
whatWouldHelp: A written **cut date**, paid teaching time and a vacancy with a workable rota would help.
